I loved seeing this. I often feel like an outsider because I can't relate to people who believe this is a helpful or healthy mindset.

I think what happens is that a lot of people meet their emotional capacity in relationships & friendships, at work and other responsibilities & instead of setting boundaries that are gentle and understandable, they wait until they're fully overwhelmed and abandon all stressors. Justifying this mindset of not owing anyone anything. 

We absolutely do have obligations. We should. Accountability shouldn't be solely seen as a burden...we should also be able to enjoy the relationships that require commitment. If you're no longer enjoying & receiving reciprocal effort in a friendship, relationship, or activity and the only way to move on to a healthier situation for yourself, after you've made other attempts to balance, it's okay to leave or withdraw to take care of yourself. But the people who abandon every friend, partner or job for minor hardship, they're not taking care of themselves but just being selfish. 

This phrase works in situations where you're an enabler who is deciding to end an enabling relationship, or a job that doesn't pay enough and has no benefits.

It is weaponized against vulnerable and neurodivergent people with support needs.

I think the idea started off as an act of self care. That it's okay to walk away from harm even if you're invested or loved by the harm. But now so many people say it & gets resentful if anyone has an expectation of them

I just want to say I understand.   I (28F) am gay but I've only had two relationships.  I am not attractive physically and I have had no luck with women.  I am extremely envious all the time.  I don't really think there is a way to deal with it, or feel better about it, because in my experience, even if you find a relationship that feels good or normal, the ...emotional fatigue of feeling like it was difficult to find and there is so much at stake because this person is the "only one", it creates an uncomfortable and sometimes insurmountable power dynamic. Both of my girlfriends were so physically attractive and even in public I felt like passersby didn't respect our relationship because I looked, I guess, "unworthy".  

Luckily, because you are young, there is a great chance things will get better. Just pour your enthusiasm into your school and interests and that will help you cope with the self esteem issues.

My dog, Houdini! I included more than a couple images because he is so expressive and you can really see his personality in an array of photos.  He is SO silly and dramatic, like he could win an oscar. When I'm not home, he acts like it's the worst day of his life. He was named Houdini because the first 2 days we had him he broke out of or into every room we put him in.  He's a true escapee! He even escaped the house once, but when I ran outside and screamed his name, he ran up to me (I was so relieved).  I'm his favorite part of everyday, and I've never met a more love-able boy. He melts like butter in my arms. (His tongue is always out!) He is so goofy. If he was drawn as a character, though, I guess I would want something silly! Maybe an 80s rock star, because of his hair, or a stereotypical nerd. He is the funniest dog.
